Applied PR #1328 ("Make Converter a kind of adapter, fix converters.pipe"):

- **`src/attr/_compat.py`**: added `PY_3_11_PLUS`.
- **`src/attr/_make.py`**: `Converter.__init__` now builds a proper `self.__call__` adapter (based on `takes_self`/`takes_field`) so `Converter` instances are directly callable and copy the wrapped converter's return-type annotation; `pipe()`'s inner loop now calls `c(val, inst, field)` instead of the broken dict-based arg lookup that was passing the boolean flags themselves as arguments.
- **`src/attr/setters.py`**: `setters.convert` now detects a `Converter` instance and calls it with `(new_value, instance, attrib)` instead of just `(new_value)` — this is what made `attrs.setters.convert`/`on_setattr` crash when paired with `converters.pipe()`.
- Added the corresponding upstream tests to `test_converters.py` and `test_setattr.py`, plus `changelog.d/1328.change.md`.

Verified byte-for-byte against the real 24.2.0 release (which shipped this exact fix) and ran the full test suite (1328 passed; the only 2 failures are a pre-existing, unrelated environment artifact from the editable dev-version install, reproduced identically on the unmodified baseline).
